rationale: The Shootout hash benchmark is a small, hot-loop workload dominated by integer/string hashing and table probing, so per-function profiling is unavailable and a conservative, cost-gated profile is safest. SUB is prioritized because arithmetic substitution yields strong static-analysis resistance on the arithmetic-heavy hash computation at near-zero size cost and minimal correctness risk. SPLIT is nearly free and adds diversity, so it gets moderate weights with very low cost sensitivity. FLA and BCF are useful against control-flow recovery but are runtime-expensive on branch-intensive hash lookups, so their cost weights are raised so they apply only to functions where the runtime/size features tolerate them. IBR and IGV are the heaviest and riskiest transforms (indirect dispatch, potential miscompilation of computed gotos and interprocedural state), so they keep high security weights but are strongly gated by RuntimeCost, SizeCost, and CorrectnessRisk so they only fire on cold, non-critical functions; ICALL is similarly allowed at moderate strength as a lighter alternative for call-graph obfuscation.
